title: Corner: Founder Pilot Mode -- First 3 Customers Without Waiting
summary: How to close Corner's first 3 paying customers at $3,500/month without waiting for S1-S3 engineering fixes. White-glove founder pilot model. AOM does the setup manually. Revenue starts before self-serve works.
content:
Corner: Founder Pilot Mode

The Problem with the Current Activation Card

Every activation document I've written gates on S1-S3. "Don't text anyone until the auth bypass is removed, the /onboarding route is fixed, and the hardcoded DEFAULT_PROJECTS are gone." That's the right call for self-serve scale. For the first 3 customers, it's a trap.

S1-S3 block self-serve signups. They don't block a founder selling directly.

The insight: Patrik can close the first 3 deals at $3,500/month without S1-S3 existing. Here's how.

The Founder Pilot Model

What It Is

Patrik sells a "Founder Pilot" -- a premium, white-glove onboarding experience for the first cohort of customers. AOM personally sets up their Corner instance. The pitch: "You won't set yourself up. We set you up. You walk in and everything is already running."

This is not a workaround. For B2B SaaS selling to owners and operators, white-glove onboarding at the $3,500/month price point is actually the right product experience. Self-serve is for the future. Founder pilots are the gold standard for early customers.

Why It Works Right Now

  • Patrik shows the product on screen-share. Prospect doesn't touch the product until it's set up for them.
  • Patrik manually creates their Supabase account with correct auth (no bypass). S1 doesn't matter -- Patrik does the setup manually and does it right.
  • Patrik manually seeds their project data. S3 doesn't matter -- no new-user auto-populate, because Patrik is doing a manual setup.
  • /onboarding 404 doesn't matter -- Patrik walks them through setup via Zoom, not through the wizard. S2 doesn't matter.

S1-S3 block self-serve. Patrik is the onboarding flow for the first 3 customers.

The Pilot Pitch

Add this to the discovery call and demo script:

"We're doing a limited founder pilot -- 5 companies max. You'd be in the first cohort. We personally set up your Corner instance: your agents, your projects, your workflows. Most companies just give you software and documentation. We give you a running system from Day 1. The pilot price is $3,500/month."

The "founder pilot" framing:

  • Justifies white-glove setup (it's the product, not a workaround)
  • Creates scarcity (5 companies max)
  • Removes the "I'll set it up later" objection (because AOM sets it up)
  • Positions AOM as a partner, not a vendor

The Pilot Setup Process

When a pilot customer signs:

Week 1 (Patrik runs this):

  1. Intake call (45 min) -- Patrik asks: What are your top 3 business problems right now? What tasks eat your time most? Who do you communicate with most? What does "winning" look like in 90 days?

  2. Account creation -- Patrik creates a Supabase user entry manually. Correct auth, no bypass. Uses their business email. Sets up their company profile.

  3. Office build -- Based on the intake call, Patrik builds their office: which agents they get, what rooms exist, what their project list looks like. Uses real data from their business (client names, current projects, recurring tasks).

  4. Seed tasks -- Patrik populates their Right Now list with 5-7 tasks that are actually relevant to their real workload. When they log in, they're not looking at empty state or demo data -- they're looking at their own work.

  5. Orientation Zoom (30 min) -- Patrik walks them through the product with THEIR data on screen. They feel like it was built for them because it was.

Week 2: Customer is live. Patrik checks in weekly for Month 1.

Total Patrik time per pilot customer: ~4 hours in Week 1, ~1 hour/week after. For $3,500/month, that's a strong return on time.

Pricing the Pilot Right

Don't discount for white-glove. Charge full price or more.

Pilot pricing: $3,500/month (same as Growth tier)

Justification: The white-glove setup is standard at this tier -- you're just making it explicit. Later, when self-serve works, you can offer a lower-touch tier. For now, everyone is a pilot.

If a prospect pushes back on price, the response is:

"At $3,500/month, we're saving you 10-15 hours a week of coordination, follow-up, and admin work. You're hiring a team that works 24/7. Your first month's cost is covered by your first week of time savings."

Do not lower the price. Do not offer a trial. The pilot framing is the offer.

The Gate Is Actually Lower Than You Think

What you need before texting the first person:

  • Corner exists and runs
  • Patrik knows the product cold (he built it)
  • Pricing is set
  • Discovery call script exists (corner-discovery-call.md)
  • Demo script exists (corner-demo-script.md)
  • One-pager exists (corner-one-pager.md)
  • Supabase can create a user account manually

What you don't need yet:

  • S1 (sessionStorage) -- white-glove setup doesn't use the bypass
  • S2 (/onboarding route) -- white-glove doesn't use the signup wizard
  • S3 (DEFAULT_PROJECTS) -- white-glove seeds real data manually
  • /corner page redesign -- the demo is live, the page just needs to not embarrass you
  • Demo environment at /demo -- Patrik IS the demo for pilot customers

The gate: Patrik knows the product and has 30 minutes.

That's it. That gate was cleared the day Corner launched.

The 3-Customer Pilot Path

Week 1:

  • Build the 15-person warm list (corner-first-10-tracker.md)
  • Send 3 Tier 1 texts per day for 5 days
  • Conduct discovery calls with everyone who replies

Week 2:

  • Run demos (Patrik's Corner, live, on screen-share)
  • Offer the Founder Pilot at $3,500/month
  • Target: 1-2 pilot signups by end of week 2

Week 3:

  • Complete setup for Pilot Customer 1 (intake, account, office, seed tasks, orientation)
  • Continue texting Tier 2 list
  • Target: Customer 1 live on Corner

Week 4:

  • First $3,500 check clears
  • Repeat for customers 2 and 3
  • S1-S3 engineering in parallel -- when they ship, offer self-serve access to active pilots

The shift: S1-S3 go from "revenue blocker" to "scale unlock." First money doesn't wait on them.

What Changes When S1-S3 Ship

Once Bobby closes S1-S3, the pilot model evolves:

  • New customers can use the self-serve signup (they still get a setup call from Patrik, but the wizard works)
  • The /onboarding wizard handles account creation (Patrik reviews it, not runs it manually)
  • No more "KOHRS" in new accounts
  • The sales cycle gets shorter (prospects can explore the product before the demo)

But by the time S1-S3 ship, you already have 1-3 paying customers. That changes everything about the sales conversation. You're no longer pitching a product -- you're inviting people to join a platform with existing customers.

Summary

Self-Serve Model (post-S1-S3) Founder Pilot Mode (now)
Ready when S1-S3 confirmed live TODAY
Setup by Customer self-serves Patrik does it manually
Onboarding time 10 min wizard 4 hrs Patrik Week 1
First revenue After S1-S3 ship This week
Price Same Same ($3,500)
Conversion rate Lower (cold product) Higher (personal trust + done-for-you)

Start pilot mode today. Migrate to self-serve when engineering is ready.

The first text goes out the day you read this. Not the day S1-S3 ship.
